metadata.case_name: CHAN CHIN SHUN v. YAU SIN CHUNG

plaintiff.occupation_after: decoration worker (painting houses and sometimes clearing debris)
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: caretaker, shopkeeper or petrol station attendant

injuries.description: Mild bifrontal contusion and contusion in the frontal region of the brain
source: A CT brain scan showed mild bifrontal contusion and a non-displaced fracture in the right mastoid bone.
There was a small patch of hyperdense opacity over the left frontal area of the brain which was compatible with brain contusion.
“blunt injury to his head with ... contusion frontal region of his brain as shown by CT scan.”

injuries.description: Non-displaced fracture in the right mastoid bone / fracture right temporal bone
source: A CT brain scan showed mild bifrontal contusion and a non-displaced fracture in the right mastoid bone.
“blunt injury to his head with fracture right temporal bone and contusion frontal region of his brain as shown by CT scan.”
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of other specified skull or facial bones

injuries.description: Scalp haematoma behind his right ear in the right occipital region
source: Behind his right ear in the right occipital region, there was a scalp haematoma.

injuries.description: Two small lacerations over his left lip and face
source: Two small lacerations were found over his left lip and face.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: Right facial weakness (facial nerve involvement) observed four days after the incident
injuries.body_part: facial nerve / muscles of the face
source: Four days after the incident he was found to be suffering from right facial weakness which responded to a short course of cortico steroids.

injuries.description: Severe hearing impairment in the right ear
injuries.body_part: right ear (hearing apparatus / cochlea and vestibule related to temporal bone)
source: He was assessed by the hospital's ear, nose and throat (“ENT”) surgeons to have sustained severe hearing impairment in the right ear.

“The organs for hearing and balance, cochlea and vestibule respectively are also situated in the temporal bone. Therefore fracture of the temporal bone can result in ... hearing loss, tinnitus and vertigo.”

“There is no effective treatment for his hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo, loss of taste and smell because the pathology lies in the respective neural pathways. The damage to nerves is difficult to recover and therefore Mr Chan's present conditions are expected to be permanent.”
injuries.icd_description: Injury of middle or inner ear

injuries.description: Complete loss of sense of smell and taste (anosmia and ageusia)
source: He was found to have completely lost his sense of smell and taste.
“Injury to the frontal area of the brain could cause loss of smell because the delicate organ of the smell lies in this region.”
“There is no effective treatment for his ... loss of taste and smell ... Mr Chan's present conditions are expected to be permanent.”

manifestations.description: Unconscious or at least semi-conscious after the blow
Totally confused (receptive dysphasia) and talked incoherently on arrival at hospital
Complete loss of smell and taste (anosmia and ageusia)
Irritability which affects his relationship with his family
Impaired concentration and memory; very limited short-term memory
Significant loss of hearing in the right ear
Attempts to concentrate cause physical pain in the head; reading leads to headaches and dizziness; difficulty tolerating heat and cold

treatments_received: physiotherapy (visits to Physiotherapy Department at Yan Chai Hospital)
treatments_future: visits to family physician (estimated five times a year over two years)

losses.description: Significant loss of hearing in the right ear
Complete loss of sense of smell and taste (anosmia and ageusia)
Impaired concentration and memory; very limited short-term memory
Irritability which affects his relationship with his family
Handicap in the labour market; difficulty obtaining employment and diminished earning capacity

losses.category: Loss of ability to enjoy quiet or solitude

losses.description: Irritability which affects his relationship with his family

comparable_cases.case_name: Chan Kwok Wai v. Secretary for Justice
